栽.meaning: A retired knight has no more battles, so he uses his old <part>halberd</part> as a garden tool: stab, twist, drop in a baby <part>tree</part>, stamp. By autumn the whole hillside is ruled in neat green rows. He made a <kanji>plantation</kanji> with a weapon.
栽.on: At harvest he presses the apples into jugs of fizzy <sound>ci</sound>der.

酬.meaning: Years ago a quarry owner lent the whole <part>state</part> his last stick of <part>dynamite</part> to blast a tunnel for its railway. Now the governor turns up with a box tied in a bow: a brand-new stick, plus a crate of fireworks as interest. The state has come to <kanji>repay</kanji> him.
酬.on: Under the fireworks lies one giant golden <sound>shoe</sound>, the state's highest thank-you.
酬.kun: His pet <sound>moo</sound>se and his <sound>coo</sound>k each get a firework too.

亀.meaning: In a park race, a <part>boomerang</part> zooms out and back a hundred times, while its rival plods along trailing a <part>plug</part> on a long cord, looking for a socket to recharge. Somehow the slow one crosses the line first. Never bet against a <kanji>tortoise</kanji>.
亀.on: Round its neck hangs a big brass <sound>key</sound> for winding itself up.
亀.kun: The <sound>ca</sound>lm winner gets a gold <sound>me</sound>dal hung on its shell.

縄.meaning: A farmer's electric fence runs out of wire, so she braids <part>thread</part> and dry straw into a long cord and ties a <part>plug</part> on the end, pushing it into the barn socket. Nothing hums, but the cows are fooled and keep well back from the <kanji>straw rope</kanji>.
縄.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops over and uses it as a skipping rope.
縄.kun: At noon she unties a bit to wrap up her picnic: a <sound>na</sound>an and a jar of <sound>wa</sound>sabi.

松.meaning: The town lets anyone use its <part>public</part> <part>tree</part> as a hairbrush: people walk up and comb their hair against its stiff green needles. It keeps its spikes all winter, so the queue never ends at the town's <kanji>pine tree</kanji>.
松.on: Every evening the freshly combed townsfolk put on a <sound>show</sound> beneath it.
松.kun: A <sound>ma</sound>ma gets a needle up her nose in the queue and sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

姫.meaning: A bowing <part>servant</part> spends all day carrying one <part>woman</part> over puddles, because her slippers are made of spun sugar and melt in the wet. She thanks him with a sticky wave. Only a <kanji>princess</kanji> wears shoes made of candy.
姫.on: Her tower opens with a big brass <sound>key</sound> that the servant keeps on his belt.
姫.kun: In the summer <sound>hea</sound>t her slippers <sound>me</sound>lt anyway.

柳.meaning: A cowboy rides up to a <part>tree</part> by the river and pushes through its long hanging branches as if they were <part>saloon doors</part>; they swing shut behind him with a swish. Inside it's cool and green, and his horse orders a lemonade. The saloon is a weeping <kanji>willow</kanji>.
柳.on: Every summer the cowboys hold a family <sound>reu</sound>nion in its shade.
柳.kun: '<sound>Ya</sound>hoo!' yells a cowboy, tossing <sound>na</sound>an to the <sound>gee</sound>se by the water.

輩.meaning: Two old <part>car</part> mechanics share one lunch every day: a single grilled fish. One eats the head end, one the tail end, and they leave the <part>fishbone</part> on the bonnet like a trophy. Forty years, one fish a day, never a quarrel. Each is the other's <kanji>comrade</kanji>.
輩.on: When bees build a <sound>hi</sound>ve in the engine, they share the honey too.
輩.kun: For pudding they split a <sound>bu</sound>ttery <sound>ru</sound>m cake, crumbs and all.

覇.meaning: In the wild <part>west</part>, one rancher wears a <part>leather</part> hat so wide it shades the whole valley, and at night he even claims the <part>moon</part>: his brand is burnt right on it. Every town, every cow, every star is his. That's <kanji>hegemony</kanji>.
覇.on: Only one tiny <sound>hu</sound>t refuses to sell, and its owner just waves.
覇.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he laughs over a <sound>ta</sound>co with <sound>ga</sound>rlic, as his <sound>shee</sound>pdog <sound>ru</sound>ns the herd.

蛮.meaning: An <part>insect</part> rides a <part>jellyfish</part> up the beach like a war horse, roaring, kicking over sandcastles and eating everyone's picnic with its bare feet. The seagulls flee. Nobody invited this <kanji>barbarian</kanji>.
蛮.on: It grabs a sticky <sound>bun</sound> and stuffs it in whole.
蛮.kun: Then it tries to juggle an <sound>e</sound>gg, a <sound>bee</sound>hive and a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi, and drops all three.

脇.meaning: Three <part>strongmen</part> pose under the <part>moon</part> with their arms raised high, oiled and tanned from head to toe. The moonlight finds the one pale patch each of them missed, and the whole crowd giggles at it: the <kanji>armpit</kanji>.
脇.on: The strongest one shouts where they tour next, '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!', stretching its start as long as his flex.
脇.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' squeals the smallest strongman when a <sound>kee</sound>n fan tickles him there.

滴.meaning: A paper <part>hanging lantern</part> sways in a cave. <part>Water drops</part> gather on the rock above, slide down its string and fall from its tassel, plink, into a cup a hermit holds out. He has waited an hour for one sip. One <kanji>drip</kanji> at a time.
滴.on: He sends a <sound>tex</sound>t message to a friend: 'Nearly half a cup!'
滴.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p, escaped from the <sound>zoo</sound>, wanders in and licks the drip off his <sound>coo</sound>king pot.

椅.meaning: A carpenter finds a <part>strange</part> <part>tree</part> in the woods: its trunk bends into a seat, two branches curve round like armrests, and four roots stand like legs. She just saws it off at the ground and carries it home. No nails needed for this <kanji>chair</kanji>.
椅.on: Her pet <sound>ee</sound>l curls up on its seat every evening.

慎.meaning: A champion boxer wins every match, but when the crowd chants his name, his <part>heartbeat</part> stays slow and his face stays quiet. 'It's <part>true</part>, I won,' he says, 'but my gran still beats me at chess.' His <kanji>humility</kanji> is his best move.
慎.on: He even says sorry to the rival whose <sound>shin</sound> he bumped.
慎.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes into his glove, then quietly says sorry to a <sound>shee</sound>p in the front row.

吉.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> crosses a pond by standing on a frog's wide-open <part>mouth</part>, and the frog doesn't mind a bit. On the far bank he finds a four-leaf clover and a gold coin in the same step. Some days are pure <kanji>good luck</kanji>.
吉.on: A <sound>kit</sound>ten follows him home, purring, to make it a full set.
吉.kun: He celebrates with a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt and lets a passing <sound>shee</sound>p lick the lid.

膚.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> visits a tattoo parlour and asks for stripes on her <part>stomach</part>, the only plain bit of her. The artist shaves a little patch and gasps: the stripes are already there underneath, printed on her <kanji>skin</kanji>.
膚.on: She pads home and naps on a striped <sound>fu</sound>ton.
膚.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the artist, putting down her needle. '<sound>Da</sound>rling, nature beat me to it.'

緯.meaning: A spider decorates a <part>pagoda</part> for a festival. She strings <part>thread</part> from eave to eave, tier after tier, every line running flat from side to side, never up or down. From far away the tower looks striped like a sweet, every stripe <kanji>horizontal</kanji>.
緯.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l climbs out of the moat and wriggles along the lowest line.
緯.kun: Spilling <sound>yo</sound>gurt, a <sound>ko</sound>ala swings along the lines, squeals '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' and lands on the <sound>to</sound>p tier.

堤.meaning: A fussy grandmother builds a wall of <part>soil</part> along the river with a teaspoon, patting each scoop until it's <part>just so</part>. When the flood arrives, it takes one look at her neat work and turns back. Never argue with a granny's <kanji>dike</kanji>.
堤.on: Where it leaks, she patches it with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
堤.kun: A <sound>tsu</sound>nami hits it, then a second <sound>tsu</sound>nami, and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat on top just keeps watch.

侮.meaning: A snooty doorman checks <part>every</part> coat before it may touch his gold <part>coat hook</part>. Too muddy, too cheap, too last year: he flicks them onto the floor with one finger and a curled lip. His whole job is <kanji>scorn</kanji>.
侮.on: A <sound>bu</sound>lldozer driver arrives in overalls, and the doorman sneers at him too.
侮.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' he sniffs at a guest holding a <sound>na</sound>an and a toy <sound>do</sound>lphin. 'No snacks, no toys.'

孝.meaning: An old javelin thrower can't bend down to pull out his <part>stuck javelin</part> any more, so his grown-up <part>child</part> runs out after every throw, tugs it free, carries it back and rubs Dad's sore knees. That's <kanji>filial piety</kanji>.
孝.on: Afterwards Dad buys them both an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.

漆.meaning: A furniture maker taps a <part>sap tree</part> and catches its sticky drips, then thins them with <part>water drops</part> until it shines like dark honey. She brushes coat after coat onto a plain box until her cat hisses at its own reflection. That glossy skin is <kanji>lacquer</kanji>.
漆.on: She lays a clean bed <sound>sheet</sound> over the box so the dust can't stick.
漆.kun: Then an <sound>u</sound>don chef, a kanga<sound>roo</sound> and a <sound>shee</sound>p queue up to check their hair in the shiny lid.

呈.meaning: A shy <part>king</part> won't show off his treasures, so his hat does it for him: it's shaped like a giant <part>mouth</part> and calls out each jewel's name as he lays them on a velvet table in the square. Crowds gather to gawp at the royal <kanji>display</kanji>.
呈.on: He marks a line on the cobbles with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe so nobody touches.

珠.meaning: A <part>king</part> goes diving in a <part>vermilion</part> wetsuit, red as a lobster, so the oysters will think he's a crab and open up. One yawns, and he plucks out a gleaming white <kanji>pearl</kanji>.
珠.on: Back home he nearly drops it in his tea, thinking it's a lump of <sound>su</sound>gar.
珠.kun: At dinner it rolls into his <sound>ta</sound>co, and his <sound>ma</sound>ma nearly eats it.

宴.meaning: A <part>woman</part> hosts dinner up on her flat <part>roof</part> for the whole street. Tables groan with pies and soup, neighbours keep climbing the ladder with more chairs, and the <part>sun</part> stays up late to watch, refusing to set until pudding. It's the town's biggest <kanji>banquet</kanji>.
宴.on: Late guests arrive on a tractor, its <sound>en</sound>gine roaring up the street.
宴.kun: Bowls of <sound>u</sound>don and plates of <sound>ta</sound>cos keep coming for every <sound>gue</sound>st.

錠.meaning: A dragon wants to <part>determine</part> exactly who can touch her <part>gold</part>, so she melts one coin into a heavy little box with a keyhole and hangs it on her treasure chest. Only she can open it now. Her best guard is a <kanji>lock</kanji>.
錠.on: A cheeky <sound>jo</sound>ey picks it with a hairpin anyway.

森.meaning: One lonely <part>tree</part> on a hill keeps calling down to the <part>grove</part> below: 'Come up, there's sun!' The two trees shuffle up roots-first and stand beneath it, and every seed they drop does the same. Soon the hill is dark, deep and full of owls: a <kanji>forest</kanji>.
森.on: A hiker bangs her <sound>shin</sound> on a root in the dark.
森.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>ssy owl hoots down at her from a <sound>ree</sound>dy hollow.

桑.meaning: A baker hangs three <part>pretzel</part> twists on a <part>tree</part> as a joke. By morning silkworms have crawled up to nibble the leaves, and dark purple berries have grown between the knots. She tastes one and stains her whole chin: a <kanji>mulberry</kanji>.
桑.on: She scrubs her purple chin with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap, but it stays purple.
桑.kun: Her <sound>coo</sound>k sees the purple chin and cries, '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

顕.meaning: A magician's <part>rubber duck</part> sits on a dark stage. Two <part>candles</part> flicker and puff out, a drum rolls, and a hidden <part>sun</part> lamp flashes on: suddenly a rabbit is sitting beside the duck. 'Ta-da!' In this act, things just <kanji>appear</kanji>.
顕.on: Next a puppy pops out of an empty <sound>ken</sound>nel.
顕.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the crowd as a <sound>ki</sound>wi, a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men and a <sound>ca</sound>rp turn up too: plain to see.

塊.meaning: A <part>ghost</part> tries to haunt a farmer's field but keeps tripping over the same hard ball of <part>soil</part> the plough left behind. It kicks it, glides through it, moans at it, but the dirt won't budge. Even ghosts can be beaten by a <kanji>clod</kanji>.
塊.on: In the end it ties the clod to a <sound>ki</sound>te to fly it away, and the kite crashes.
塊.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in the ditch eats a <sound>ta</sound>co and watches, while its <sound>ma</sound>ma hides behind a <sound>ree</sound>d.

幣.meaning: A street sweeper finds an old <part>rag</part> wrapped round a bundle and dries it on a <part>towel</part>. As it unfolds, notes flutter out: twenty, fifty, a hundred, soggy but real. She pegs each one up on the washing line. Her garden is full of <kanji>cash</kanji>.
幣.on: A horse in the barn sneezes, and more soggy notes blow out of its pile of <sound>hay</sound>.
幣.kun: The last note goes in a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k behind a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.
